chokhmat_shlomo.he: סעיף א' הישן תחת המטה בסוכה. נ"ב גרסינן בש"ס בסוכה פ"ב דף... הישן תחת המטה בסוכה לא יצא י"ח אר"י נוהגין היינו שהיינו ישינים תחת המטה וכו'. והנה פי' רש"י והרע"ב פירשו דהטעם דמטה הוי אוהל עראי דמטלטלת ממקום למקום. והנה הראו לי בתוי"ט שם שהקשה מ"ט לא פליג ר' יהודה בקינופות לעיל ברפ"א מ"ג והניח בצ"ע. ולדעתי א"ש דזה דומה למ"ש בשבת גבי זרק ונח בפי כלב חייב אף דבעינן הנחה על מקום ד' מ"מ מחשבתו משויה ליה מקום א"כ מוכח דמהני אחשביה לעשותו כמו מקום חשוב. אך אחשביה לא מהני רק ממה דדרך בני אדם לעשות כן אבל מה דאין דרך בני אדם לעשות כן לא מהני אחשביה וכמ"ש רפ"ג דפסחים גבי כותח הבבלי הנח לכותח הבבלי אי בעינא קאכיל בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם ע"ש. ולכך א"ש דבשלמא בקינופות כיון דאחשביה לאהל ודרך בני אדם לעשות כן מהני בזה אחשביה ומורה ר"י דמחשבתו משוויה ליה אוהל. אך זה אם ישן על המטה דדרך בני אדם לעשות כן אבל הישן תחת המטה דאין דרך בני אדם לעשות כן בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם ולא מהני מחשבתו וממילא הוי רק אוהל עראי ולא מבטל אוהל קבע. והנה שאלני אחד דהרי מפורש שם די"א ומביאו התוי"ט במקומו דגם בכילת חתנים פליג ר"י וזה הוי דרכו בכך ופליג וא"כ למה לא פליג בקינופות. והנה תחלה עלה בלבי לו' דבשלמא כילת חתנים י"ל דאינו מכוין לשם אוהל רק לצניעות וכעין דאיתא בש"ע הלכות שבת סי' שט"ו דהיכי דהוי לצניעות בעלמא אין בו משום אוהל כן ה"נ הוי רק לצניעות ואין ראיה דאחשביה לאוהל אבל אם ישן לבדו תחת המטה או בקינוף זה אינו לצניעות רק לאוהל לכך בזה יש חילוק בין היכי דדרכו בכך ובין אין דרכו בכך. מיהו שבתי וראיתי דא"ש יותר דהמשנה דפ"ק מפורש שם שפירס סדין על גבי קינוף א"כ מוכח דהוא בוחר בזה ורוצה לעשות אוהל לכך בזה אחשביה אבל בכילת חתנים דהכילה נעשה כבר ואינו עושה עתה בידים א"כ יתכן להיות דבלי הכילה נמי היה ישן א"כ ל"ש אחשביה לכך פליג ר"י ובמטה אף דמניח עצמו לישן תחת המטה וחזינן דבוחר באהל זה מכל מקום בזה כיון דאין דרכו בכך בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם וא"ש בעזה"י ומ"ש לעיל סי' תרכ"ו ס"א אם השפיל הענפים למטה עיין במקור דין זה בש"ס פ"ק דסוכה ד"ט בפירש"י בד"ה בשחבטן שכתב דמדאורייתא ברובא בטל. הנה מה שנשאלתי על לשון מדאורייתא ומה שהשבתי בזה עיין בהשמטות להלכות נדרים סי' רט"ו מ"ש בזה דרך אגב למשכיל אחד בלבוב ע"ש כי שם קנה מקומו ודו"ק:
chokhmat_shlomo.en: Se'if 1 One who sleeps under a bed in a sukkah. Note: We read in the Talmud, Sukkah chapter 2, that one who sleeps under a bed in a sukkah has not fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Yehudah said: it was our practice that we would sleep under the bed, etc. Rashi and the Bartenura explained that the reason is that a bed is a temporary ohel, for it is moved from place to place. They showed me the Tosafot Yom Tov there, who asked why Rabbi Yehudah does not disagree regarding kinofot above at the beginning of chapter 1, Mishnah 3, and he left it requiring examination. In my opinion this is understandable, for it resembles what is written in Shabbos regarding one who threw and it landed in a dog's mouth: he is liable, even though we require resting on an area of four, because his intention gives it the status of a significant place. This proves that treating something as significant can make it like an important place. But treating something as significant helps only where it is something people normally do; where people do not normally do so, his intention is nullified relative to everyone else, as written at the beginning of the third chapter of Pesachim regarding Babylonian kutach: leave Babylonian kutach aside; if he wants to eat it, his intent is nullified relative to everyone. Therefore it works well. With kinofot, since he treated it as an ohel and people normally do this, his intent is effective, and Rabbi Yehudah agrees that his thought gives it the status of an ohel. But this is only if he sleeps on the bed, which people normally do. One who sleeps under a bed does something people do not normally do, so his intent is nullified relative to everyone and it is only a temporary ohel, which does not nullify a fixed ohel. Someone asked me: it is explicit there that some say, and the Tosafot Yom Tov cites it in its place, that Rabbi Yehudah also disputes regarding a bridal canopy, and that is its normal manner; if so, why does he not dispute regarding kinofot? At first I thought to answer that with a bridal canopy, one can say he does not intend it as an ohel, only for privacy, like what is stated in Shulchan Aruch, Laws of Shabbos, siman 315, that where it is only for privacy there is no prohibition of ohel. So too here it is only for privacy, and there is no proof that he treated it as an ohel. But where he sleeps alone under the bed or under a kinof, this is not for privacy but for an ohel; therefore in that case there is a distinction between where this is the normal manner and where it is not. However, I returned and saw that it works better this way: the Mishnah in the first chapter explicitly says that he spread a sheet over a kinof, so it is proven that he chooses this and wants to make an ohel; therefore he treated it as significant. But with a bridal canopy, the canopy was already made and he is not now making it by hand; it is possible that he would have slept even without the canopy, and therefore treating it as significant does not apply, so Rabbi Yehudah disagrees. With a bed, although he places himself to sleep under the bed and we see that he chooses this ohel, nevertheless, since this is not the normal manner, his intent is nullified relative to everyone. This is understandable, with God's help. What I wrote above in siman 626:1 regarding if he lowered the branches below, see the source of that law in the Talmud, first chapter of Sukkah 9, in Rashi s.v. beshechavtan, who wrote that by Torah law it is nullified by majority. Regarding the question I was asked about the wording by Torah law, and what I answered about this, see the omissions to the Laws of Vows, siman 215, where I wrote about this incidentally to an insightful person in Lvov; see there, for that is its proper place. Consider this.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק א) אם כו' ועיין סי' שט"ו ותראה שיש ט"ס בדבריו. ר"ל דהאגודה הביא ראיה מסי' שט"ו ושם כ' להיפך בסעיף י"א וז"ל שם והוא שלא תהי' משולשלת מעל המטה טפח. אולם הטעם מבואר שם כיון שהכילה פרוסה לצל הוי המטה עשוי' כעין גג באמצע המחיצה של הכילה. מה שמשולשל למטה הוי מחיצה. מכל מקום אין ענינו שייך לכאן. בשלמא לעיל סי' שט"ו דמיירי לענין איסור עשיית אהל בשבת א"ש דכה"ג אסור דהוי אהל. אבל הכא דמיירי לענין הישן שם דמיקרי אינו ישן בסכה דאהל מפסיק. א"כ מה בכך דתחת המטה נקרא אהל. הא הוא ישן ע"ג המטה ושם ליכא אהל מפסיק. ואי בישן תחת המטה בלא"ה אסור כדאי' ריש הסי':
machatzit_hashekel.en: (Se'if katan 1) If, etc. See siman 315 and you will see that there is a scribal error in his words. Meaning, the Agudah brought a proof from siman 315, but there it is written the opposite in se'if 11, in this wording: provided it is not lowered from the bed one tefach. However, the reason is explained there: since the canopy is spread for shade, the bed is made like a roof in the middle of the canopy's partition. What is lowered below is a partition. Nevertheless, that matter is not relevant here. It works well above in siman 315, where the subject is the prohibition of making an ohel on Shabbos; in such a case it is forbidden because it is an ohel. But here, where the subject is one who sleeps there and whether he is called not sleeping in a sukkah because an ohel interrupts, what difference does it make that under the bed is called an ohel? He is sleeping on top of the bed, and there no ohel interrupts. And if he sleeps under the bed, that is forbidden in any case, as stated at the beginning of the siman.

And behold there is room to question how wide the sekhakh below and above should be, and if one inserted four pegs and put sekhakh on them below the upper sekhakh with air between lower sekhakh and walls — some say the lower is nullified and validated by the upper; others say whenever the lower has more shade than sun, upper sekhakh does not help at all and one sits in the lower without walls and does not fulfill; but if lower is properly covered with walls and sekhakh above on the roof breach without walls, or upper lacks four handbreadths of valid sekhah measure — the lower is validated, for in any case upper is not fit for sukkah — not "sukkah under sukkah," since it also requires ten handbreadths height and all sukkah validity — understand and requires study.

Even if we emend the text to read, and also the sheets do not reach, etc., nevertheless there the reason for the prohibition is that the bed is like a roof in the middle of a canopy, and it is forbidden to stretch it out because under the bed there would be an ohel. But here, where he sleeps under the canopy and not under the bed, what do the sheets matter? However, it seems that the Agudah holds that whenever the partitions reach the ground, even though within less than three tefachim there is not a width of one tefach near the top, it is nevertheless an ohel. This also seems from the Agudah's words in Shabbos, chapter Tolin, where he wrote: or he should not make the roof one tefach wide within three tefachim, and also the walls should not reach the ground; if he makes it this way, he may sleep under it in the sukkah, as written, etc. There is a scribal error here, and it must read: and also the sheets do not reach there, as I wrote above. His words imply that both are required: the roof should not be one tefach wide, and additionally the walls should not reach the ground. But from the words of Tosafot and the other poskim it does not seem so. According to the version in Agudah in Sukkah, where he wrote: if it has no roof, such as where it is not one tefach wide within three of its roof, and also the sheets that reach the ground do not have a partition of one tefach, even though it is ten high it is permitted to sleep in it, etc., it would appear that the text should read: and also the sheets do not reach the ground; there is no partition of one tefach. In our Magen Avraham the text reads, that they do not have a partition, implying it refers to the sheets, but this is a scribal error and should read, that it does not have, referring to the canopy. So it is in the Bach. Meaning, since the roof has no tefach, automatically even if the sheets reach the ground, nevertheless there is no partition of one tefach here, because sloping tents are not treated as tents. But the Agudah's words in Shabbos require examination. See Mekor Chayim, where it should read Agudah. See the Bach in siman 315, and you will see, etc.; but this is not so. Afterwards I saw in the Machatzit HaShekel that he seems to have understood that what the Magen Avraham meant by siman 315 is what is written in the Shulchan Aruch: and if it is lowered from the bed, etc. But this is not so, as I wrote above, for that is not relevant here, and he himself wrote this. For this reason, with a bed there is certainly a roof above the one lying beneath it, one tefach wide or more, and ten tefachim high, meaning from the roof over the sleeper down to the ground. Otherwise, even though the bed as a whole is ten tefachim high, it is valid. In letter 1 and in the Bach the dispute is mentioned. It implies that according to the Rif, Rambam, and Rosh, one who sleeps under the bed is invalid by Torah law like sukkah beneath a sukkah, for this also applies to invalid s'chach: the bed is invalid because it was not made for shade but to lie upon, and even if it was set up for shade, it is rabbinically invalid when it is four tefachim distant because of the decree of a ceiling. According to the Razah, it is rabbinic, because it appears that he is standing in the shade of an ohel and not in the shade of the sukkah. A practical difference is on the first night, if he has no place except under the bed; see Tosafot and the Yerushalmi regarding Tavi. See siman 629, Magen Avraham 22, and the general introduction: with something rabbinically invalid, if he has no other, he performs the mitzvah and by Torah law fulfills it, and perhaps even blesses, because in such a case they did not decree. There we wrote that one can distinguish between a decree and something that appears as marit ayin or the like. Also on the second night, he would not recite shehecheyanu. According to the one who says the invalidity is Torah-level, in such a case he does not sit under the bed on the first night, and on the second night he recites the time blessing. However, even according to the Rif, Rambam, and Rosh one can say that it is not Torah-level invalidity but rabbinic, because it resembles sukkah beneath a sukkah. The Bach did not write this, and it requires examination in practice. One who studies the Milchamot will see that sukkah beneath a sukkah is when the upper s'chach is invalid s'chach that is not for shade, for there is a lower one; and according to Shmuel in Sukkah 10a, why do I need ten tefachim between them? See the Ramban about this, and Rashi on the Mishnah.

In my humble opinion one can say that the Magen Avraham was precise in the wording of the Shulchan Aruch, which changed from the Gemara's wording. In the Gemara it says: provided that the naklitin are not ten tefachim higher than the bed. In the Shulchan Aruch it says: provided that they are not ten high. This implies that it refers to the naklitin themselves, that they should not be ten high. The Magen Avraham was troubled: the Gemara's wording works well, that the naklitin should not be ten higher than the bed, implying that if they are not ten higher than the bed, even though the naklitin themselves are ten high, for example where the naklitin are fixed in their middle and part of the naklitin is below the bed, it is still permitted, since in any event they do not extend above the bed ten tefachim and do not have the law of an ohel. But the Shulchan Aruch wrote simply, provided they are not ten high, meaning the naklitin, even though they are not ten higher than the bed, as where they are fixed in the middle as above; nevertheless it has the name of an ohel. On this the Magen Avraham was troubled: why should it have the name of an ohel? Therefore the Magen Avraham was forced to say that each source took the usual case of its time. In the time of the Talmud, the naklitin were fixed in the bed and had the law of one who supported his sukkah on the legs of the bed, where it cannot stand on its own. Then we do not measure from the ground but from the bed floor, and therefore the baraita required that the naklitin be ten tefachim higher than the bed floor. But in the time of the Beit Yosef, the way was that the naklitin were not fixed in the bed but in the ground next to the bed. Then they have the law of a sukkah that can stand on its own, like one who placed s'chach on pegs, in which case the ten tefachim are measured from the ground. Therefore the Shulchan Aruch made the measure depend on the naklitin themselves, whether they are ten high, even if there are not ten from the bed floor. The Magen Avraham's words are thus understandable.

biur_halacha.he: ואם אינו לנוי וכו' - זה הלשון איתא ג"כ בטור והוא נובע מן דברי הרא"ש ע"ש ור"ל דלאו דוקא מפני הנשר פסולה דאפילו שלא מפני הנשר כל שאינו לנוי פסול דלא בטיל לגבי סוכה ועיין בביאור הגר"א דכלל בזה אם פירס הסדין כדי לנגבו דהוא צורך הבגד דפסול וצ"ע דלפ"ז סותר הטור א"ע דבסימן זה פסק דלצורך הבגד פסול ובסוף סימן תרכ"ט מוכח דס"ל דלצורך הבגד שרי כמו שכתב הד"מ שם ועל השו"ע עצמו אף דהוא העתיק ג"כ בסוף סימן תרכ"ט לשון הטור וכונתו בודאי להקל אף בשעת אכילה וכמו שהוכחנו שם לא קשה לי דאפשר דדבריו שם לא קאי רק לדברי הי"א שהביא מתחלה דהוא שיטת ר"ת ולדידיה ודאי שרי לצורך הבגד כמו שכתבו האחרונים ולא לדעה ראשונה הנזכר שם בתחלה אבל הטור דלא זכר שם רק דעה זו בלבד קשה [ומצאתי בדברי הב"ח בסימן זה שכתב וז"ל וע"ל סוף סימן תרכ"ט דס"ל לרבינו דלאו דוקא לנוי אלא ה"ה נמי כשהניח לצורך האדם להגן עליו או לשאר צורך דין נוי יש לו עכ"ד ומוכח מיניה דמש"כ הטור ואם אינו לנוי היינו שלא היתה לצורך כלל דזה פסול מדינא אבל לצורך הבגד ה"נ דשרי וכ"כ בהדיא בסוף סימן תרכ"ט ע"ש אבל לפי דברי הגר"א צ"ע] ואולי י"ל בדוחק לפי מה שכתב הגר"א דהמחבר בסימן תרכ"ו ס"א שכתב דבכ"ז לא שאני לן בין שהאילן קדם ובין שהסוכה קדמה סתם כדעה הראשונה ודלא כשיטת ר"ת והנה זה הלשון כתב ג"כ הטור שם ע"ש ולפ"ז ניחא דהטור בסימן תרכ"ז אזיל לפי מה שהעתיק לדינא בסימן תרכ"ו דלא כשיטת ר"ת שאין שום יתרון במה שהסוכה קדמה כיון שהסדין היתה צילתה מרובה מחמתה ולפ"ז להגן מפני החמה והעלין אסור וס"ל דה"ה מפני צורך הבגד ג"כ אסור וכאן שהעתיק בפנים שיטת ר"ת סיים דמפני הבגד ג"כ שרי. ועל עיקר הענין מפני מה בסימן תרכ"ו העתיק לדינא דלא כשיטת ר"ת וכאן העתיק שיטת ר"ת כבר תמה הב"י. ועיין בב"ח ובהגהות מהרל"ח:
biur_halacha.en: And if it is not for beauty, etc. - This wording is also found in the Tur, and it derives from the words of the Rosh; see there. It means that it is not specifically because of falling leaves that it is invalid, but even not because of falling leaves, anything not for beautification is invalid, for it is not nullified to the sukkah. See the Biur HaGra, who includes in this one who spread the sheet in order to dry it, which is the need of the garment, that it is invalid. This requires examination, for according to this the Tur contradicts himself: in this siman he rules that for the need of the garment it is invalid, while at the end of siman 629 it is proven that he holds that for the need of the garment it is permitted, as the Darchei Moshe wrote there. Regarding the Shulchan Aruch itself, although he too copied the Tur's wording at the end of siman 629 and his intent there is certainly to be lenient even at the time of eating, as we proved there, it is not difficult for me. Perhaps his words there refer only according to the some say view that he first brought, which is Rabbeinu Tam's approach, and according to that view it is certainly permitted for the need of the garment, as the later authorities wrote, and not according to the first opinion mentioned there at the beginning. But the Tur, who mentions there only this view, is difficult. I found in the Bach here that he wrote: see below at the end of siman 629, where our teacher holds that it is not specifically for beauty, but the same applies when he placed it for a person's need, to protect him, or for another need; it has the law of beautification. These are his words. It is proven from him that when the Tur wrote and if it is not for beauty, he means that it was not for any need at all, and this is invalid by law. But where it is for the garment's need, it is indeed permitted, as he wrote explicitly at the end of siman 629; see there. But according to the Gra's words, this requires examination. Perhaps one can answer with difficulty according to what the Gra wrote, that the Mechaber in siman 626:1, where he wrote that in all this there is no difference between whether the tree preceded or the sukkah preceded, ruled plainly like the first opinion and unlike Rabbeinu Tam. This wording is also written by the Tur there; see there. According to this it works well: the Tur in siman 627 follows what he copied as practical law in siman 626, unlike Rabbeinu Tam, that there is no advantage in the sukkah having preceded, since the sheet had more shade than sun. According to that, protecting from the sun and leaves is forbidden, and he holds that the same applies for the garment's need. But here, where he copied Rabbeinu Tam's approach inside, he concludes that for the garment's need it is also permitted. The Beit Yosef already wondered about the main matter: why in siman 626 he copied the law unlike Rabbeinu Tam, while here he copied Rabbeinu Tam's approach. See the Bach and the glosses of Maharlach.

(9) If he spread a sheet, etc. The same applies if he decorated it with other kinds of things that may not be used as s'chach, such as if he hung beneath all the s'chach foods and attractive vessels in order to beautify it.
(10) It is valid - For they are nullified to the s'chach, and it is permitted even to sit beneath them.
(11) And if it is four tefachim distant, etc. - Since they are four tefachim distant from the s'chach, they are considered independent and are not nullified to the s'chach. It turns out that he is not sitting in the shade of the sukkah, but in the shade of the sukkah decorations. Even if those decorations have more sun than shade, it is also forbidden. (12) It is invalid - This is when they have a measure of four tefachim, which is like other invalid s'chach whose measure is this, as below in siman 632. If it is in the middle, it invalidates the whole sukkah for this reason, as explained there.
(13) And if it is not for beauty, etc. - See the Biur Halacha.
(14) Even though it is within four tefachim - The same applies even if it is not one tefach distant from the s'chach; he mentions four because of the first clause.
(15) And one must be careful, etc. - Meaning, although by law one need forbid only where there is a width of four tefachim, as above, nevertheless initially one should be careful even if it is not four tefachim wide, for there is concern that he may make many decorations until they have this measure and sit beneath them. According to this, one should not hang fruits, vessels, or similar items that are invalid for s'chach, even for decoration, except within four tefachim of the s'chach. Nevertheless, regarding hanging lamps in the sukkah opposite the table, one need not be stringent that they be within four tefachim; on the contrary, it is better and proper to distance them from the s'chach as much as possible.
